'''Primož Brezec''' (born October 2, 1979) is a Slovenian former professional [[basketball]] player. He is a 7 ft 1 in (2.16 m) tall [[center (basketball)|center]]. Brezec has played eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].

==Professional career==

===Europe/Asia===
Brezec grew up in [[Sežana]], where he also made his professional debut with the local team Kraski Zidar. During his high school years, he was a member of the basketball team and a major star of the ŠKL League, the national high school league. As a professional, he played for the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian Premier A League]] club [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija Ljubljana]] from 1998 until 2001.

Brezec spent the next 7 seasons playing in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] in the United States and Canada. He returned to Europe on July 20, 2008, when he signed a 2-year contract with [[Lottomatica Roma]] of the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian league]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/euroleague/news/|title=Latest News | EuroLeague|date=October 19, 2023|website=Euroleague Basketball}}</ref>

On September 26, 2010, Brezec signed with [[BC Krasnye Krylya Samara]] of the [[Russian Professional Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hoopsleader.com/news/brezec-is-moving-to-russia/|title=Brezec is moving to Russia | HoopsLeader.com|date=July 12, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110712215720/http://hoopsleader.com/news/brezec-is-moving-to-russia/ |archive-date=2011-07-12 }}</ref>

In July 2011, he signed with [[Lokomotiv Kuban]] for one season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/86878/lokomotiv-kuban-lands-center-brezec|title=Lokomotiv Kuban lands center Brezec - Latest - Welcome to Eurocup|date=February 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210170112/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/86878/lokomotiv-kuban-lands-center-brezec |archive-date=2015-02-10 }}</ref> but he was waived in February 2012.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/35842/lokomotiv-kuban-waived-primoz-brezec.html Lokomotiv Kuban waived Primoz Brezec]</ref>

In March 2012, he signed with [[BC Nizhny Novgorod]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/36133/primoz-brezec-moves-to-nizhny-novgorod.html Primoz Brezec moves to Nizhny Novgorod]</ref>

On February 10, 2015, he signed a two-month deal with [[AEK Larnaca B.C.|AEK Larnaca]] of the [[Cyprus Basketball Division 1]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/cyprus/151814/primoz-brezec-moves-to-aek-larnaca.html|title=Primoz Brezec moves to AEK Larnaca}}</ref> He won the title in Cyprus with AEK Larnaca averaging 14.9 points and 7 rebounds per game.

On May 7, 2015, after his contract expired, he signed with [[Kuwait SC (basketball)|Al Kuwait]] of the [[Kuwaiti Division I Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/160481/primoz-brezec-signs-with-al-kuwait.html|title=Primoz Brezec signs with Al Kuwait}}</ref>

On June 18, 2015, he re-signed with AEK Larnaca.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/cyprus/164640/primoz-brezec-returns-to-aek-larnaca.html|title=Primoz Brezec returns to AEK Larnaca}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, he announced his retirement from professional basketball,<ref>{{cite web|title=Brezec retired and become a scout for the Cavs|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/505774/brezec-retired-become-scout-cavs/|website=Eurohoops|access-date=September 12, 2017|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref> and joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as international scout.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Vardon|first1=Joe|title=Isaiah Thomas' road to a comeback with Cavaliers begins Tuesday in Cleveland|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2017/09/isaiah_thomas_road_to_a_comeba.html|website=cleveland.com|access-date=September 12, 2017|date=September 1, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Taningco|first1=Brad|title=Cavs news: Cleveland will add Primoz Brezec to staff as international scout|url=https://cavsnation.com/cavs-primoz-brezec-international-scout/|website=cavsnation.com|access-date=September 12, 2017|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

===NBA===
[[File:Primoz Brezec.jpg|thumb|left|95px|Brezec with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in 2006.]]
Brezec was chosen by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 27th overall pick of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. After he spent three years in Indiana with little playing time, he was picked up in the [[2004 NBA expansion draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. As the Bobcats' starting center, Brezec averaged career-highs of 13.0 points and 7.4 rebounds per game during the [[2004–05 NBA season]]. He also scored the first points, made the first turnover, and hit the first free-throws in the history of the franchise. After the season, he would re-sign on a three-year, $8.25 million contract.

On December 14, 2007, Brezec, along with Bobcats teammate [[Wálter Herrmann]], was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] for center [[Nazr Mohammed]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3155460|title=Bobcats acquire forward Mohammed from Pistons|date=December 15, 2007|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

At the 2008 NBA [[trade deadline]], which was on February 21, Brezec, along with cash considerations, was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Juan Dixon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3257496|title=Raptors acquire well-traveled Brezec from Pistons|date=February 21, 2008|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> During his Raptors debut, he hit all five of his shots and finished with 11 points, three rebounds and a block in 13 minutes off the bench against the [[New York Knicks]] in a February 24 win.

In August 2009, he returned to the NBA when he signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/08/13/76ers.brezec.ap/index.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150727212133/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/08/13/76ers.brezec.ap/index.html|url-status=dead|title=Center Brezec returns to NBA, signs contract with 76ers|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=July 27, 2015}}</ref>

On February 18, 2010, Brezec was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with [[Royal Ivey]] in exchange for [[Jodie Meeks]] and [[Francisco Elson]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks_sixers_100218.html |title=Bucks Acquire Ivey, Brezec from 76ers |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-02-18 |access-date=2010-02-18}}</ref> His final NBA game was played on May 2, 2010, in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference First Round against the Atlanta Hawks. The Bucks lost the game 74 - 95, (thus losing the series) with Brezec recording 5 points and 2 rebounds.

==National team career==
[[File:Slovenia vs. Serbia at EuroBasket 2009 (08).jpg|thumb|Brezec (#7) at [[EuroBasket 2009]]]]
